title: Social Protection, Inclusion and Empowerment
description: The project aims to enhance the resilience of the most vulnerable populations in Syria through the revitalization of financial, human, and social capital, thus fostering participation in recovery and peacebuilding processes.It leverages three interrelated streams:1- Social Protection and Inclusive Socioeconomic Empowerment: Aims to revitalize financial and human capital through financial aid, healthcare, economic empowerment, and skill development, with particular attention to women, persons with disabilities, and youth.2- Social Inclusion: Addresses inequalities by promoting human rights, inclusive policies, and practices focusing on women, youth and persons with disabilities.3- Social Cohesion: Strengthens trust within communities (horizontal dimension) and between society and institutions (vertical dimension). It includes creating platforms and forums for dialogue, community centers, and fostering values like diversity and empathy.

title: Community Infrastructure Rehabilitation
description: Pillar II: Basic services rehabilitationThe project addresses major service delivery problems and basic infrastructure rehabilitation to contribute to the early recovery, improve living conditions for people in the affected areas, help accelerate the return of the IDPs to their homes, and the revitalization of basic business services in the targeted areas. These projects target affected communities through the rehabilitation of social buildings (schools, hospitals, health centers, shops, bakeries, civil service centers, vocational training centers, and Museums…) and the rehabilitation of sewage, water, and irrigation networks, especially in high-priority areas in different governorates.

title: Local Peace Building and Community Resilience

title: Post-earthquake emergency debris removal
description: The project will be removing 100,000 M3 of rubble from the streets, to restore full access to basic services for the affected populations in Harim district. This project will engage male and female workers from the affected population in a CFW scheme. The debris and rubble removal will be planned and documented by remote sensing technology which provides high-resolution satellite images comparing the situation pre- and post-earthquake, in collaboration with UNOSAT, to accurately identify the number of buildings affected. title: MPTF Joint PhaseII
description: Brief DescriptionThe Joint Programme applies a nuanced, area-based, and conflict-sensitive approach, ensuring that community participation is optimized. This includes targeted efforts for the inclusion of conflict-affected and marginalized groups, such as women, youth, people with disabilities and the elderly.UNJP 2.0 is a collaborative initiative that brings together the combined expertise and capacities of six UN agencies: FAO, UNDP, UNFPA, UN-Habitat, UNICEF, and WFP. The programme aims to achieve the following overarching objectives:•	Improving equitable access to essential services such as electricity, water, education, and healthcare.•	Restoring sustainable livelihoods and food systems, fostering long-term resilience and economic stability.•	Enhancing social protection, building trust, and improving governance to create a robust and inclusive foundation for community development.UNDP will contribute to the UNPJ through the rehabilitation of electricity network, provision of solar energy, debris management, support of HLP and revive of the livelihoods.

title: Energy for Resilience in Syria-ECHO
description: This project aims to reduce access to electricity has severely impacted all aspects of daily life in Syria, particularly in conflict-affected urban and peri-urban areas. This project aims to strengthen the resilience of communities by enhancing access to stable and reliable electricity which is critical for access to essential services and improving economic conditions. The project will focus on the installation of eight electrical trans-formers along with medium and low voltage distribution networks in three locations in Damascus and Rural Damascus governorates. These installations will restore electricity to critical community infrastructure including health centers, schools, water pumping stations, as well as workshops and residential areas, directly benefiting thousands of vulnerable people and supporting early recovery. In addition, the project includes the installation of two solar photovoltaic systems to ensure uninterrupted electricity supply for two key health centers: Sbeineh Health Center, and Daraya Health Center. These PV systems will provide sustainable, clean energy and improve access to essential health services in the face of frequent grid outages, to support the provision of medical services for the inhabitants in the targeted areas. In total, the Action will address the immediate needs and challenges of electricity supply for 432,000 residents in the targeted areas
